title: The Oldest Mountains in Europe
lead: A park in the Holy Cross Mountains. Quartzite boulder fields, the monastery on Holy Cross, and beech forests that remember geological epochs.
body:
The Oldest Mountains in Europe

Holy Cross National Park is a park in the Holy Cross Mountains — one of the oldest mountains in Europe, estimated at over 500 million years old. These are mountains completely different from the Tatras or Karkonosze — gentle, forested, but full of unique geological and natural phenomena.

The park is famous for its boulder fields — rock rubble formed during the Ice Age when frost shattered quartzite rocks. The boulder fields cover the steep slopes of Łysa Góra and Łysica — the two highest peaks of the Holy Cross Mountains. It is worth seeing them up close — the rubble is impressive in its sheer scale.

Holy Cross and the Fir Forest

At the summit of Łysa Góra is the monastery on Holy Cross — one of the oldest sanctuaries in Poland, where relics of the Holy Cross are kept. For centuries the monastery was a place of pilgrimage for kings and nobles — today it is open to tourists and pilgrims.

The park is also the Fir Forest — one of the most valuable forest complexes in Poland, where firs over 200 years old grow. It is worth walking through the forest — this is one of the few places in Poland where the forest looks primeval.
tip: Climb Łysa Góra from Nowa Słupia — the route is easy, and the views of the boulder fields are delightful. It is also worth visiting the monastery on Holy Cross.
